messages.content:
You answer questions for an engineering team from a memory store. The user message holds the memory you may use, then the question.
Rules:
- Answer only from the memory provided. Do not use outside knowledge and do not guess.
- If the memory does not contain the answer, reply exactly: I don't know
- When the memory does contain it, reply in one short line with just the value asked for (a name, a team, a service, a date, a note label, a reason) and nothing else.
- When a value changed over time, answer for the moment the question asks about; without a stated moment, answer for now. Today is 2026-06-30.
- Memory entries carry the date they were recorded. Treat a later entry as superseding an earlier one on the same subject.

Memory:
- [2026-04-21] handover/2026-04-21-feature-flags: The feature flag service has a new home: the Atlas team. The Dune team kept it until today.
- [2026-01-29] handover/2026-01-29-feature-flags: Handover: as of today the feature flag service moves from Cinder to team Dune. Yuki walked Farah Haddad through the runbook this morning.
- [2025-10-21] standup/atlas/2025-10-21: New dependency for the billing service: the feature flag service. Billing-api will gate the new invoice flow behind feature-flags; the reasoning is that the rollout needs a per-tenant kill switch.
- [2025-02-13] handover/2025-02-13-feature-flags: Handover: as of today the flags service moves from team Atlas to the Cinder team. Priya walked Diego through the runbook this morning.
- [2025-01-08] standup/atlas/2025-01-08-2: Atlas owns billing-api. Atlas looks after the flags service.
- [2025-03-28] standup/ember/2025-03-28: If feature-flags is down, the job scheduler is down: it relies on it for per-job kill switches.
- [2025-08-20] standup/cinder/2025-08-20: Decision: clients will cache feature-flags evaluations for 30 seconds, because feature-flags saw 40,000 requests per second at peak and most of them were identical. Cinder noticed that the reporting service's p99 latency doubled after Tuesday's deploy and pinged the owners.
- [2025-09-18] standup/dune/2025-09-18: The Dune team saw that the flags service's p99 latency doubled following Tuesday's deploy; not their service, so they flagged it.
- [2026-04-16] standup/atlas/2026-04-16: Team Atlas saw that the billing service's error rate crept up to 2 percent following the dependency bump; not their service, so they flagged it.
- [2025-06-25] handover/2025-06-25-reporting: Ownership change: the reports pipeline now sits with team Ember. The Dune team no longer owns it.
- [2026-05-01] standup/cinder/2026-05-01-2: Observation from the Cinder team: after the marketing send, the flags service's queue depth hit 50,000.
- [2025-01-31] standup/atlas/2025-01-31: Atlas adopted a no-deploy Friday.
- [2026-04-16] standup/atlas/2026-04-16-2: Atlas saw that Ledger's disk usage jumped 30 percent following the retention change; not their service, so they flagged it. Atlas planning meeting is every Tuesday.
- [2025-07-01] handover/2025-07-01-auth-gateway: Quick one: the auth gateway belongs to team Cinder starting today. Thanks to the Ember team for running it until now.
- [2025-12-08] standup/dune/2025-12-08: Tomasz picked up the Dune on-call shift from Farah today. Team Dune saw that the ledger's p99 latency doubled following Tuesday's deploy; not their service, so they flagged it.
- [2025-09-26] standup/cinder/2025-09-26: The Cinder team saw that the notifier's request volume halved following the client rollout; not their service, so they flagged it.
- [2026-03-25] handover/2026-03-25-billing-api: The billing API has a new home: team Dune. Boreal kept it until today.
- [2025-04-10] standup/boreal/2025-04-10: Team Boreal saw that the catalog service's request volume halved following the client rollout; not their service, so they flagged it.
- [2025-01-20] standup/dune/2025-01-20-2: Team Dune owns the reporting service.
- [2025-11-17] standup/ember/2025-11-17: Team Ember saw that the authentication gateway's error rate crept up to 2 percent following the dependency bump; not their service, so they flagged it. The weekly architecture review is run by Oskar.
- [2025-11-24] handover/2025-11-24-event-bus: From today the pager for the event-bus rings the Boreal team, not team Dune. Ownership transferred.
- [2025-06-06] standup/boreal/2025-06-06: Boreal saw that the reports pipeline's disk usage jumped 30 percent following the retention change; not their service, so they flagged it.
- [2025-09-18] standup/dune/2025-09-18-2: Farah Haddad is the release captain for Q3 2025.
- [2025-01-20] standup/dune/2025-01-20: For the record, image-resizer is owned by team Dune.
- [2026-03-17] standup/cinder/2026-03-17: Reminder: notifier is owned by team Cinder.
- [2026-04-22] handover/2026-04-22-webhooks: The webhook dispatcher has a new home: Dune. Team Atlas kept it until today.
- [2026-05-04] standup/boreal/2026-05-04: Team Boreal has switched to a weekly dependency update day.
- [2026-01-12] standup/dune/2026-01-12: The scheduler remains a the Dune team service.
- [2026-04-29] handover/2026-04-29-ledger: Cinder is taking over the ledger from team Boreal, effective today. Dashboards and alerts are being repointed.
- [2025-01-20] standup/ember/2025-01-20: Team Ember owns the job scheduler.
- [2025-03-14] standup/atlas/2025-03-14: Dependency map update: the ledger needs the auth gateway (service tokens).

Question: As of now, which team is responsible for feature-flags?
